_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: As-Designed Parts, Materials, and Processes List (ADPMPL)
summary: Specifies a complete listing of EEE parts, materials, COTS products, and processes used to manufacture a complete end item, used to track supply chain, product change, and non-conformance impacts.
use_relationship:
The As-Designed Parts, Materials, and Processes List (ADPMPL) is a complete listing of: the electrical, electronic, electromechanical, and mechanical parts; materials; Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) products; modified COTS products; and processes used in the manufacture of a complete end item.  The ADPMPL Data Item Description (DID) describes this requirement for a piece of equipment or system that is approved and selected for design.   Unless stated otherwise by the work task described in the contract, the government intends to use the ADMPL to track potential impacts due to, but not limited to, supply chain issues, product change notices, and non-conformance or potential non-conformance information from the Government Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP), industry, or program alerts and advisories.

This DID contains the format, content, and intended use information for the data deliverable resulting from the work task described in the contract.

Definitions
Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Products: Commercial items that typically require no unique government modifications or maintenance to meet the needs of the procuring agency, during the life cycle of the product.  Examples include Versa Module Eurocard (VME) boards, hard drives, and computers.  If a source control drawing has been developed with specific requirements for an item, it is not considered COTS.
Electrical, Electronic, and Electromechanical (EEE) Parts: The term "electronic" part is used in a broad sense and includes electrical, electromagnetic, electromechanical, and electro-optical parts.  This definition includes any part that can carry, store, or transmit electrical current, or electromagnetic or optical waves in the intended application.  EEE parts include capacitors, connectors, crystal oscillators, diodes and transistors, fiber optics, filters, fuses, hybrid microcircuits, monolithic microcircuits, magnetics, relays, resistors, thermistors, wire, and cable.
Material: Material is a metallic or nonmetallic element, alloy, mixture, or compound used in a manufacturing operation that becomes a permanent portion of the manufactured item, or which can leave a remnant, residue, coating, or other material that becomes or affects a permanent portion of a manufactured item.
Mechanical Part: The term mechanical piece parts (non-electrical parts) is used in a broad sense and includes such simple mechanical items as nuts, bolts, washers, pins, terminals, and discrete parts (other than required as an accessory in EEE Parts herein), that cannot be disassembled into their component sections without rendering them unfit for their intended use.  Such mechanical piece parts have a single, non-electrical function (other than electrical grounding) and contain one or more necessary material items.  Formed, machined, shaped or otherwise fabricated items such as brackets, enclosures, etc., and processed portions of packages used by electronic assemblies, with no electrical circuitry, ground plane, or thermal functions are considered mechanical parts.
Part: A hardware element that is not normally subject to further subdivision or disassembly without destruction of functional use.  Examples include resistor, integrated circuit, relay, connector, bolt, and gasket.
Process: An operation, treatment, or procedure used as a step in the manufacture of an item.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference Documents
preparation_instructions.content: This DID has no reference documents.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content:
The ADPMPL data shall be in electronic spreadsheet workbook format in accordance with the ADPMPL Cover Page and its instructions for use (see Tables 1 and 2 below). Three data spreadsheets within the same workbook shall be used to enter all of the data. These spreadsheets shall be labeled "EEE Parts", "Materials and Processes", and "Mechanical Parts".  The proper spreadsheet, pertinent to each specific part type, shall be used to enter the data.
Only data for one part shall be entered in each spreadsheet row.   For example, data for identical parts from more than one manufacturer shall be entered in separate rows, one row for each part manufacturer.  Electronic media (email, electronic files, computer compact discs, etc.) shall comply with DoD Instruction 8320.02 ("Sharing Data, Information, and Information Technology (IT) Services in the Department of Defense," August 5, 2013) and be readable by approved Government systems.

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: ADPMPL data shall include all the parts, materials, processes, COTS products, modified COTS products, and the corresponding data fields identified as being required in Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 below.  The data fields and their values shall be in accordance with the corresponding Data Field Description in Table 1 below.  The word "parts" refers to electrical, electronic, and electromechanical (EEE) parts and mechanical parts.
